title: JWT signing and validation
summary: How JSON Web Tokens are issued, signed with RS256, and validated in our API gateway.

content.overview: A JWT is a compact, URL-safe token consisting of three base64url-encoded segments: header, payload, and signature. We use RS256 (RSA + SHA-256) so that services can validate tokens with the public key without holding the signing key.
content.details: Issuance: the auth service holds a private RSA key and signs a payload containing sub, iat, exp, aud, and any role claims. Lifetime is 24 hours; refresh is handled separately. Validation at the gateway: (1) decode header, confirm alg=RS256 and a known kid, (2) fetch the corresponding public key from the JWKS endpoint, (3) verify the signature, (4) check exp, nbf, aud, and iss. Rotate keys by adding a new kid to JWKS before retiring the old one.
content.examples: Decoded header: {alg: RS256, kid: 2026-q2, typ: JWT}. Decoded payload: {sub: user_123, iat: 1716800000, exp: 1716886400, aud: api.example.com, roles: [user]}.
content.caveats: Never accept alg=none. Reject HS256 tokens at gateways that expect RS256 (algorithm-confusion attack). Do not store sensitive PII in the payload — JWTs are signed but not encrypted. Set short exp; rely on refresh tokens for long sessions.
